summary:
Astragro is a multilingual, NASA-powered farming intelligence platform that turns live Earth-observation data into clear, explainable decisions for any farm on Earth — with no sensors to buy and no account to create.

Farmers everywhere make irrigation and crop decisions almost blind, while NASA satellites continuously measure rainfall, heat and soil moisture over their fields. Astragro closes that gap. A farmer picks a location on a map (or tries our Hubli, Karnataka demo farm), and Astragro fetches real NASA POWER daily observations — temperature, rainfall, humidity, solar radiation and root-zone soil wetness — alongside GPM IMERG precipitation and SMAP soil-moisture imagery via NASA GIBS, and NASA EONET environmental events.

An interactive 3D digital twin of the farm changes colour with these live observations, while climate, rainfall and soil dashboards, risk indicators and downloadable reports make trends understandable. A transparent AI advisor answers questions in English, Kannada, Telugu or Hindi — by text or voice — always showing its reasons, supporting measurements, confidence and limitations, and never inventing data.

Astragro makes satellite intelligence free, local-language and trustworthy for the smallholder farmers who need it most.
details:
WHAT ASTRAGRO DOES

Astragro is a web platform that turns live NASA Earth-observation data into clear, explainable farming decisions for any farm location on Earth. It needs no sensors, no hardware and no user account — only a browser.

HOW IT WORKS

1. The farmer selects a farm location by clicking on an interactive satellite map, searching a place name, entering latitude/longitude, or opening the built-in demo farm (Hubli, Karnataka – 15.36°N, 75.12°E). Multiple farms can be saved and switched instantly.

2. Astragro fetches real daily environmental observations for those exact coordinates from NASA: temperature, maximum/minimum temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, solar radiation and root-zone soil wetness from the NASA POWER API; precipitation imagery from the NASA GPM IMERG mission and soil-moisture imagery from the NASA SMAP mission via NASA GIBS; and nearby natural events from NASA EONET.

3. The platform analyses this data through interactive charts, monthly and period comparisons, rainfall-accumulation and consistency analysis, soil-moisture trends, and six live environmental risk indicators (soil dryness, heat stress, dry spell, frost, heavy rainfall and persistent humidity).

4. An interactive 3D digital twin of the farm changes colour according to the selected data layer (soil wetness, rainfall, temperature, humidity, stress), so farmers can literally see their field's condition.

5. A transparent AI advisor answers natural questions — "Should I irrigate my field today?" — in English, Kannada, Telugu or Hindi, by typing or by voice, and can read answers aloud. Every answer shows the recommendation, the reasons, the supporting NASA measurements, the observation date, a confidence level and honest limitations.

6. Farmers can download printable farm environmental reports (print/PDF, HTML, CSV and JSON).

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Agriculture consumes about 70% of global freshwater withdrawals (UN FAO), and about 84% of the world's farms are under 2 hectares. Smallholder farmers make irrigation and crop decisions almost blind, while free satellite data that could guide them never reaches them in an understandable form. Astragro makes NASA intelligence free, location-specific, visual and available in local languages with voice support, so even a farmer with low literacy can ask a question aloud and act on trustworthy information — reducing water waste, avoiding climate losses and improving resilience.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (React Three Fiber) for 3D, Leaflet for maps, Recharts for data visualisation, Framer Motion and GSAP for animation. Backend: Node.js, Express and MongoDB with modular NASA data services (POWER, GPM/IMERG, SMAP). Voice input/output uses the Web Speech API. Data sources: NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS, NASA EONET and OpenStreetMap/Esri map tiles. No specialised hardware is required; it runs on ordinary smartphones, tablets and computers.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN FACTORS

Our creative focus was trust and accessibility. Unlike typical dashboards that show unexplained numbers, Astragro never fabricates data: unavailable datasets are honestly labelled, forecasts are never mixed with observations, and every recommendation is explainable. We combined a cinematic video hero, an explorable 3D farm and an orbital globe view with a serious, production-grade dashboard so that judges and farmers understand the value within seconds. We designed for low-end devices (adaptive 3D quality and fallbacks), local languages and voice-first interaction, because the farmers who need this most have the least access to technology.
